subject: MerchantEdge discovery — cost & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Chen <jamie@merchantedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: MerchantEdge discovery — cost & pilot next steps

Jamie — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap while it's fresh and to align on next steps.

What we heard (pain & goals):
- Primary pain: token spend is unpredictable during peak reconciliation windows; monthly bills spike and eat into margins.
- Goal: get a validated pilot that demonstrates a path to predictable unit cost at scale (target < $0.002/query average including embeddings for fraud checks).
- Constraints: procurement needs a clear TCO and timeline (legal/infosec checklist is in flight), and infra preference is hosted for rapid start but open to Dedicated if cost/latency justify it.

Preliminary levers we discussed (what Redwood will model for you):
- Batching: micro-batching for synchronous flows and larger batch windows for async reconciliation jobs.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (templates + partial histories).
- Quantization/model variant routing for lower-cost high-throughput paths.

Attachments I said I'd share: pilot cost model (worked examples for 10k / 100k / 500k MAU), and your security questionnaire that you emailed. See attached stubs.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will send the pilot_cost_model.xlsx for your review (attached).
2) Marissa will provide a commercial sketch + SOW template and commit options for a 6–12 week pilot.
3) Karthik (SE) will run a short technical deep-dive to confirm batching feasibility and needed sample traces.
4) Procurement: Jamie, please confirm the team contact and preferred SLA/term questions so we can include them in the SOW.

Open asks from our side:
- Can you share a representative sample of query traces (anonymized) for peak and off-peak windows? Prefer CSV or newline-delimited JSON.
- Do you have an internal budget band for a pilot (ballpark)? That helps shape sizing and whether we prioritize Dedicated or Hosted options.

Thanks — I pasted a summary into HubSpot as well (link below). If this looks right, we'll schedule the technical deep-dive for next week.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

Sofia — appreciate the clear recap. High level response and a few clarifying Qs:

1) Batch vs latency: our reconciliation is mostly async but we also have a handful (~500/day) of near-real-time decisions where latency above ~350ms is noticeable. Can you confirm expected latency impact for a batching strategy that targets 80–90% token efficiency on those near-real-time flows?

2) Pilot budget: procurement is comfortable with a pilot spend in the $25k–$40k range for 8 weeks, assuming outcomes show at least 30% unit-cost improvement vs our current provider.

3) Private deployment: security flagged whether Redwood supports VPC/private deployments; if not, we may need to run the pilot under Dedicated capacity. Can you note that specifically in the SOW?

We can provide anonymized traces — we'll start the export (likely a subset of Sep 1–14) and expect to share by Friday.

One logistical note: procurement prefers line-item TCO for cloud egress and storage — can you include that template?

Thanks — I looped procurement above.

Jamie Chen
Head of ML Platform, MerchantEdge

Jamie — great context, thanks. Short answers + what we'll include in the commercial sketch/SOW:

- Latency w/ batching: for near-real-time flows we typically use adaptive micro-batching (window < 50ms) which preserves 95th pct latency within your 350ms target at modest throughput. We'll model this explicitly.
- Pilot budget: we can frame a baseline 8-week pilot within your $25k–$40k band. We’ll provide two scoping options: "LEDGER-FAST" (focus on low-latency 500/day decisions) and "BATCH-FIRST" (optimize reconciliation jobs).
- Private/Dedicated: yes — Redwood supports Dedicated pools and Private (VPC) deployments. We'll include a Dedicated option priced in the commercial appendix and an estimated delta vs hosted.

What I'll produce by EOD Friday:
- Commercial sketch + SOW template with line-item TCO (compute, storage, egress, support).
- A baseline cost example using the pilot_cost_model.xlsx Sofia attached, with scenarios for 10k / 100k / 500k MAU.

Karthik — please lead the technical deep-dive. Jamie — can we book 30 minutes next Wed (29 Sep) or Thu (30 Sep) US-PST? Karthik will list the specific trace format and a short checklist (anonymization + sample size).

Marissa Cole

Jamie / Marissa / Sofia — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive. Thanks for offering the traces, Jamie — those will be the most helpful thing for accurate TCO. A few practical points so the pilot remains within your procurement band: 

Assumptions I will model for the pilot (we'll validate with traces):
- Typical user interaction: 1.8 prompts per decision, ~240 tokens prompt avg, 80 tokens generation avg (post-edit).
- Peak concurrent inference for reconciliation jobs: assumed 120 qps batched into 64-size micro-batches for async jobs; near-real-time path will use micro-batches <= 8 to preserve latency.
- Caching: expected hit-rate 20–40% on KV/prefix cache for templated prompts in early deployment; if your templates are highly repetitive, can be higher.

Preliminary ballpark economics (illustrative, to be refined after traces):
- Baseline hosted (no batching/cache optimizations): $0.0065 per decision.
- With batching + caching + a lower-cost model variant for bulk work: ~$0.0035 per decision (~46% improvement).
- Dedicated pool (reserved commit) could reduce unit cost further depending on utilization; I'll include a break-even utilization table in the deck.

Deliverables before the deep-dive:
- Short checklist for traces + anonymization (attached).
- A one-page pilot sizing table (10k / 100k / 500k MAU) and an ops playbook for switching between hosted/dedicated mid-pilot.

Request: please upload a 48–72 hour sample of peak traces (anonymized) to the Drive link Sofia included. If that's not possible, a CSV with timestamp, prompt_length, response_length, latency_ms is sufficient.

I'll hold Wed 29 Sep 10:00–10:30 PST for the deep-dive; Marissa, please confirm or propose an alternate.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
